about.title: Riverside Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: When a hospital stay or clinic visit in Riverside leaves you worse off than when you arrived, the first question is usually not about lawyers. It is about what went wrong and whether anyone will explain it. We exist for the moment after that, when you decide you want an attorney to look at your records. Our team handles medical negligence cases on contingency. California's MICRA rules shape every one of these claims: a one-year clock that starts when you discover the harm, a hard three-year outer limit from the date of injury, a 90-day notice you must send before filing, and a cap on non-economic damages that increases each year. Nearly every case also needs a qualified medical expert to say the care fell below the standard. That is why a bad result by itself is not enough; we have to show the provider did something a careful one would not have done.

items.title: The MICRA clock is short and starts quietly
items.desc: In California you generally have one year from when you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. An early consultation gives us room to gather records before that window narrows.

items.title: The 90-day notice is handled before filing
items.desc: California requires written notice to each provider at least 90 days before a malpractice lawsuit is filed. We build that step into the timeline so it does not become a surprise.

items.title: Expert review comes before promises
items.desc: A qualified medical expert is almost always needed to show the care fell below the accepted standard, because a poor outcome alone is not malpractice. We will tell you honestly whether the medicine supports a claim.

items.question: I was treated in a Riverside emergency room after a crash on I-215 and they missed a fracture. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Possibly, but it depends on what a reasonable emergency physician would have caught with the information available that night. Riverside recorded 1,995 injury collisions in 2025, and emergency departments see a steady flow of crash patients, especially on Friday evenings. A missed injury becomes a malpractice claim only when a qualified expert concludes the standard of care was not met. We can obtain your imaging and chart and have it reviewed.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California places a statutory cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering, and that cap rises each year under MICRA. Economic losses like medical bills, lost wages, and future care are handled separately. We can explain how the current cap applies to the year your claim is filed.

items.question: How do I get a free case review, and what does it cost?
items.answer: Contact us for a free case review. We handle medical negligence cases on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
